tr: „„Where“ is for a place.“
en: „„Where“ is for a place.“

tr: „In a letter I write „although“.“
en: „In a letter I write „although“.“

tr: Geriye bakış. Hangi olay önce oldu?
en: Looking back. Which event came first?

tr: Amaç, sonuç, ödün, en sonda üçünün adı.
en: Purpose, outcome, concession; their three names last.

tr: İki koşul ve iki kural. Hangisi gerçek?
en: Two conditions and two rules. Which one is real?

tr: Edilgen ve aktarma. Fail nerede duruyor?
en: The passive and reported speech. Where does the doer stand?

tr: Süre: pazartesi başladı ve hâlâ sürüyor.
en: A stretch of time: it began on Monday and is still here.

tr: Yasak: „must not“, „don't have to“ değil.
en: A prohibition: „must not“, not „don't have to“.

tr: „„Must“ has no past. There is no „musted“…“
en: „„Must“ has no past. There is no „musted“…“

tr: Şey, kişi, yer; en sonda sınamanın kendisi.
en: A thing, a person, a place; the test itself last.

tr: „the „not“ sits in front of the infinitive…“
en: „the „not“ sits in front of the infinitive…“

tr: İki yaşam yan yana. Hangi bağlaç isim alıyor?
en: Two lives side by side. Which linker takes a noun?

tr: Karşıtlığın üç biçimi ve duygunun iki zamanı.
en: Three shapes of contrast and two tenses for a feeling.

tr: „avoid“ „-ing“ istiyor; „avoid to walk“ olmaz.
en: „avoid“ takes „-ing“; „avoid to walk“ is not a form.

tr: Kapıdaki üç kural. Hangisi dünü anlatabiliyor?
en: Three rules by the door. Which one can speak of yesterday?

tr: „„By the time“ names a deadline, not an event…“
en: „„By the time“ names a deadline, not an event…“

tr: Amaç, sonuç, ödün. Hangi bağlaç nereye gidiyor?
en: Purpose, outcome, concession. Which linker goes where?

tr: Önce kuralı taşıyan cümle, sonra takvim sırası.
en: First the sentence that carries the rule, then the calendar order.

tr: Üç gelecek biçimi, tek kişi. Hangisi ayarlanmış?
en: Three future forms, one person. Which one is arranged?

tr: „give up“ „-ing“ istiyor; „give up to buy“ olmaz.
en: „give up“ takes „-ing“; „give up to buy“ is not a form.

tr: Aktarılan üç cümle. Hangisinde „whether“ geliyor?
en: Three reported sentences. Which one takes „whether“?

tr: Bir korkuyla yüzleşme. Hangi fiil mastar istiyor?
en: Facing a fear. Which verb takes the infinitive?

tr: Failsiz, failli, kipli; en sonda kuralın kendisi.
en: No doer, a doer, a modal; the rule itself last.

tr: Şey, kişi, yer. Hangi adıl hangi boşluğa giriyor?
en: A thing, a person, a place. Which word goes in which gap?

tr: Geçmişin iki katmanı. Hangi cümlede „had“ zorunlu?
en: Two layers of the past. In which sentence is „had“ required?

tr: Üç kural, üç ayrı iş. Hangisi geçmişe gidebiliyor?
en: Three rules, three different jobs. Which one can go to the past?

tr: Biri üzgün. Hangi kural kaldırıyor, hangisi koyuyor?
en: Somebody is sad. Which rule takes away and which one puts one there?

tr: Önce olan iş „had“ + üçüncü hâl; soru sonra geliyor.
en: The earlier thing is „had“ + third form; the question comes after.

tr: Üç ilgi cümlesi. Hangi sözcük hangi boşluğa gidiyor?
en: Three relative clauses. Which word goes in which gap?

tr: Üç bağlaç, üç ayrı iş. Hangisi yalnız geriye bakıyor?
en: Three linkers, three jobs. Which one can only look backwards?

tr: Üç edilgen, üç ayrı iş. Hangisinde fail geri geliyor?
en: Three passives, three jobs. In which one does the doer come back?

tr: Duyguyu adlandırmak. Hangi cümle çizgi, hangisi nokta?
en: Naming a feeling. Which sentence is a line and which a point?

tr: İki koşul yan yana. Hangisi gerçek olmayanı anlatıyor?
en: Two conditions side by side. Which one speaks of the unreal?

tr: Önce kuralın iki örneği, sonra vadinin kendi hikâyesi.
en: First two examples of the rule, then the story of the valley.

tr: „„Your help is appreciated“ sounds generous and is not…“
en: „„Your help is appreciated“ sounds generous and is not…“

tr: İki kişi bir nehri konuşuyor. Hangi fiil „-ing“ istiyor?
en: Two people talk about a river. Which verb takes „-ing“?

tr: Aktarma ve fiil sonrası biçim. Hangi fiil mastar istiyor?
en: Reported speech and the form after the verb. Which verb takes the infinitive?

tr: „„Decide“ takes the infinitive; „avoid“ takes the „-ing“.“
en: „„Decide“ takes the infinitive; „avoid“ takes the „-ing“.“

tr: Aktarılan üç cümle, bir dostluk. Hangisinde sıra düzleşiyor?
en: Three reported sentences, one friendship. In which one does the order go flat?

tr: „Because „tired“ asks for sleep and „sad“ asks for a person.“
en: „Because „tired“ asks for sleep and „sad“ asks for a person.“

tr: Gerçek koşul, gerçek olmayan koşul, „unless“, en sonda yargı.
en: Real condition, unreal condition, „unless“, the verdict last.

tr: „„If I was less shy“ is heard everywhere and written nowhere…“
en: „„If I was less shy“ is heard everywhere and written nowhere…“

tr: „„Unless“ carries its own negative: it means „if you do not“.“
en: „„Unless“ carries its own negative: it means „if you do not“.“

tr: „„Don't have to“ takes a rule away; „must not“ puts one there…“
en: „„Don't have to“ takes a rule away; „must not“ puts one there…“

tr: Gereklilik, gerekliliğin yokluğu, yasak, en sonda geçmiş biçim.
en: A requirement, the absence of one, a prohibition, the past form last.

tr: „the order never moves: „must“, then „be“, then the third form.“
en: „the order never moves: „must“, then „be“, then the third form.“

tr: Metnin kendi sırası: cümlecik, isim, rapor dili, en sonda kural.
en: The order of the text: clause, noun, report language, the rule last.

tr: Yol yapılmadan önce burası neydi? Hangi cümlede „had“ gerekiyor?
en: What was here before they built the road? Which sentence needs „had“?

tr: „Then there is „by the time“, and that one takes the choice away.“
en: „Then there is „by the time“, and that one takes the choice away.“

tr: „the same „who“ serves one woman and forty, a subject and an object…“
en: „the same „who“ serves one woman and forty, a subject and an object…“

tr: „„on the other hand“ only works if a first hand has already been given.“
en: „„on the other hand“ only works if a first hand has already been given.“

tr: Aktarılan soruda sıra düzleşiyor; „whether“ devrik sıranın işini üstleniyor.
en: In a reported question the order goes flat; „whether“ takes over the work of the inversion.

tr: „„Despite“ takes a noun — the distance, the snow, the rain — and never a clause.“
en: „„Despite“ takes a noun — the distance, the snow, the rain — and never a clause.“

tr: „I use „must“ where the rule is mine and „have to“ where it belongs to the company.“
en: „I use „must“ where the rule is mine and „have to“ where it belongs to the company.“

tr: „In the room she said „it is over“, and by the time I told anyone it had become „was“.“
en: „In the room she said „it is over“, and by the time I told anyone it had become „was“.“

tr: „a reported question goes flat, and „whether“ carries what the word order used to carry.“
en: „a reported question goes flat, and „whether“ carries what the word order used to carry.“

tr: „„As a result“ gives an outcome: the thing that followed, and it can only look backwards.“
en: „„As a result“ gives an outcome: the thing that followed, and it can only look backwards.“

tr: „„before“ has already put the two events in order, so the verb does not have to do it again.“
en: „„before“ has already put the two events in order, so the verb does not have to do it again.“

tr: „The feeling started when she left, which is a moment, and „started“ is the right form for a moment.“
en: „The feeling started when she left, which is a moment, and „started“ is the right form for a moment.“
